title: Sheinbaum Signs Decree to Make Government Information More Transparent and Accessible
author: Enrique Méndez and Ángeles Cruz
content:
_This article by Enrique Méndez and Ángeles Cruz originally appeared in
the[August 4, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/08/04/politica/sheinbaum-
firma-decreto-que-evita-reserva-de-informacion-de-manera-discrecional-por-
parte-de-funcionarios), Mexico’s premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City.** President Claudia Sheinbaum this morning signed a decree to
make government information more transparent and accessible for public
consultation, and to specify that the classification of documents related to
national security or matters under litigation will no longer be left to the
discretion of officials. She also reported that at the start of the
congressional session she will send an initiative to reform the Transparency
Law, so that the decree’s provisions are incorporated into the legislation on
the matter.

> “Under the current law it is established that officials can determine what
> is made public or not, depending on national security issues or matters that
> are in a judicial or administrative proceeding. **It is no longer up to the
> judgment of an official, of the secretary, of the area director of Petróleos
> Mexicanos or of the Federal Electricity Commission** ,” she said at her
> morning press conference.

The Anti-Corruption Secretary, Raquel Buenrostro, explained that the decree
has to do with strengthening the principle of maximum disclosure and
publishing government information “beyond the legal obligations.”

She noted that the decree, which will be published today in the Diario Oficial
de la Federación, is **oriented around four areas: public procurement; Pemex
and CFE subsidiaries; audits and inspections; and an invitation to states,
municipalities and other branches of government to join the maximum disclosure
policy.**

She detailed that contracts, including those of Pemex and CFE, will be
published every month, and no longer quarterly, and added that a
simplification of the 173 information classifications is planned, to reduce
them only to those related to national security and matters under litigation.
In these last two cases, public versions will be published, she specified.
